Today a drawn game counts as a loss for the first player, and the page never says how many games were drawn. So the first player can look weaker than they are: with perfectly even seats and 4% draws, it reads "First player wins 48%". After this change, the share is taken over the games somebody won, and the draw rate is shown beside it. ## Why - `GameTotal::count` (`crates/engine/src/wire/stats.rs:781-785`) adds every game to `games` and draws to `draws`. - `game_figures` takes `first_share` as `first_wins / games` and the Wilson interval over `games` as well (`stats.rs:1505`, `:1535`). A draw therefore sits in the denominator as a first-seat loss. - `apps/web/src/stats/GamesPanel.tsx:85-88` prints "First player wins {share}% (±{margin})" with no draw count. The `stats report --games` CLI reads the same computation (R1994000, "One computation"). - R1994000 built these figures so a seat decision such as R1156000's would have numbers from people's games. The opening deal has changed again since (R2368000, the first player opens on three cards). ## Proposal - In `game_figures`, take `first_share` and its Wilson interval over the decided games (`games − draws`). `GameFigures` gains a `draw_share` field. - `/api/stats/games`, `stats report --games` and the panel read these fields. The panel shows "First player wins X% of decided games (±m)" with "Y% drawn" beside it. - When every game is a draw, the share is unknown, not zero. - A new ruling in the issue's block amends R1994000. ## Where it lands - `crates/engine/src/wire/stats.rs` - `crates/tools/src/stats.rs`: the CLI line and its check of `analysis/fixtures/*.report.json`, regenerated - `apps/web/src/stats/GamesPanel.tsx` and `GamesPanel.test.tsx` - the generated wire types under `apps/web/src/wire/` - the new string in `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` - `spec/rulings/R.md` with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/.md` (§9.11) ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A unit test: 10 games with 4 first-seat wins, 4 second-seat wins and 2 draws give a first share of 0.5 over 8 decided games and a draw share of 0.2. - [ ] All draws give an unknown share without a division by zero, and the panel says so. - [ ] `stats report --games` and `/api/stats/games` give the same figures, and the committed fixture reports match the command's output. - [ ] The panel shows the draw share, and the Chinese string exists. - [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` passes. ## Size and risks Small to medium. No migration is needed, since `draws` is already in the totals. The generated TypeScript types and the fixture reports change. A reader who compared old and new figures sees the first share rise by about the draw share; the ruling says so. --- Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty.
